<reason>A won by keeping the motion’s actual target—secret person-specific markups—distinct from time, inventory, and posted deals CON kept treating as if they were banned. That left CON’s access and waste arguments mostly answered, while A’s same-shelf test, invisibility/competition point, and pressure on the “blank-slate subsidy” story stayed live. CON landed real damage on line-drawing and “lows need highs,” but overclaimed models systematically help the poor and sometimes argued a broader ban than A defended.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s first rebuttal (and later swap-the-customer answers) separating leftover-capacity/public coupons from a private WTP tax, which collapsed CON’s scarcity analogies and forced CON onto a narrower, more speculative inclusion claim.</best_rebuttal>
